svg.title: SpaceX catches Starship's upper stage with the launch tower's arms
svg.desc: Editorial illustration, seen from low on the dunes at SpaceX's Starbase site on the Texas Gulf Coast. A tall lattice launch tower rises on the right; its two long mechanical arms close around a stainless-steel Starship upper stage, dark heat-shield tiles on one side, as it descends tail-first on short landing-burn flames, its dotted return path arcing down from the sky, with steam billowing off the pad below. Behind it a huge pale sun is circled by faint orbit rings, an illustrative nod to its 14 orbits. In the foreground, silhouetted workers raise their arms and cheer. It represents SpaceX's first catch of the Starship upper stage on Nov. 14, 2026, after Flight 15.
